result.topic_en: Euler notes that his rule yields the height corresponding to the jet's velocity rather than the actual jet height, which air resistance further reduces, and proposes a table of N and M values for each ratio n of channel length to diameter so that jet height can be found as v = Nq − M.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 381
ducto ſubtrahatur numerus poſterior M, reſiduumque
exhibebit altitudinem iactus in pedibus expreſſam.

111. Hoc autem modo prodibit non tam ipſa
iactus altitudo, quam altitudo celeritati, qua aqua exſilit,
debita; conſtat enim hanc altitudinem ob reſiſtentiam
aëris inſuper aliquantum diminui, ita vt, ſi fons ver-
ticaliter exſiliat, eius altitudo aliquanto minor ſit futu-
ra, quam per regulam datam reperitur. Huius vero
diminutionis, quae ex alio fonte originem trahit, hic
nullam rationem habebo.

112. Quo igitur, quouis caſu oblato, altitudo
iactus ob frictionem ſolam imminuta facilius colligi
queat, conueniet tabulam conſtrui, quae pro quouis
valore ipſius $n$, ſeu quoti ex diuiſione longitudinis cana-
lis per eius diametrum orti, exhibeat valores litterarum
N et M. His enim inuentis, ſi inſuper altitudo caſtelli
ſupra orificium fontis $q$ in calculum trahatur, ſine negotio
altitudo iactus $v$ inde colligetur, cum ſit
$v = Nq - M$ pedum.

items.english: For it is known that this height is further diminished somewhat by the resistance of the air, so that if the fountain spouts vertically, its height will be somewhat less than is found by the given rule.

items.quote:

valore ipſius $n$, ſeu quoti ex diuiſione longitudinis cana-
lis per eius diametrum orti, exhibeat valores litterarum
N et M.
items.english: It will be convenient to construct a table which, for any value of n, i.e. the quotient arising from dividing the length of the channel by its diameter, gives the values of the letters N and M.
